runs.basis: Plain PDO, the statements Laravel would send for a savepoint, then ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT after the failure. Manual and baseline MPCS-03: with innodb_rollback_on_timeout OFF, 1205 rolls back only the statement, so the savepoint still exists and the rollback removes only the inner marker. With it ON, the whole transaction is gone: the savepoint rollback fails with 1305, the next insert autocommits, and PDO::commit() throws because that insert left no transaction.

The candidate. ConcurrencyErrorDetector matches "Lock wait timeout exceeded". At level 2, handleTransactionException lowers the level, runs the inner afterRollBack callbacks, drops the inner afterCommit callbacks and throws DeadlockException without sending ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT. OFF: the transaction and savepoint survive the 1205, so when the outer closure catches and returns, COMMIT keeps the inner marker after afterRollBack:inner has run. ON: InnoDB already rolled everything back; the next insert autocommits, PDO::commit() throws, and the outer afterCommit stays in the manager until the next commit (the laravel/framework#61964 path).
